Primality tests

Source: R/ntheory.R
isprime.Rd

isprime() tests one integer using GMP (Baillie-PSW plus Miller-Rabin rounds), so its answer is certain below 2^64 and a probable prime above, as in SymPy. is_gaussian_prime() tests a Gaussian integer. The remaining functions are the individual pseudoprime tests: Fermat, Euler and Euler-Jacobi to base a, Miller-Rabin mr() over bases, the Selfridge Lucas tests, proth_test() for Proth numbers and is_mersenne_prime(). is_square() tests for a perfect square when given an integer.

Usage

isprime(n)

is_gaussian_prime(num)

is_fermat_pseudoprime(n, a)

is_euler_pseudoprime(n, a)

is_euler_jacobi_pseudoprime(n, a)

mr(n, bases)

is_lucas_prp(n)

is_strong_lucas_prp(n)

is_extra_strong_lucas_prp(n)

proth_test(n)

is_mersenne_prime(n)

Arguments

n

An integer.

num

A Gaussian integer: an R complex number, a sym expression or an integer.

a

Base of the test.

bases

A vector or list of integer bases.

Value

TRUE or FALSE.

Details

Integer arguments may be numbers, gmp big integers, decimal strings or sym integers. Doubles at or above 2^53 are refused, because they may have lost digits already; pass a string or big integer.

Examples

isprime(97)
#> [1] TRUE
isprime("170141183460469231731687303715884105727")
#> [1] TRUE
is_gaussian_prime(complex(real = 2, imaginary = 3))
#> [1] TRUE
mr(1373651, c(2, 3))
#> [1] FALSE
